A transversal in a Latin square $L$ of order $n$ is a set of $n$ entries that contains exactly one entry from each symbol, one entry from each row, and one entry from each column relative to the square's natural ordering. In 1967, M. Hall posed the question of whether every Latin square of order $n$, where $n$ is odd, necessarily possesses a transversal. The current paper introduces a straightforward, necessary, and sufficient condition for the existence of a transversal in a Latin square. Specifically, it is demonstrated that a Latin square $L$ has a transversal if and only if, for every subset of rows $I$ in $L$ with $|I| < n$, the union of the symbols appearing in these rows, denoted as $\bigcup_{i\in I} R_i$, satisfies $|\cup_{i\in I} R_i| > |I|$.

The proliferation of mobile devices with diverse screen sizes and resolutions has heightened the demand for efficient video transcoding. This study introduces a transcoding simulation model that leverages cloud computing to enhance both scalability and cost-efficiency. The model utilizes a queueing framework to evaluate and compare the performance of two distinct cloud architectures: a homogeneous setup comprising only cloudlets, and a heterogeneous arrangement combining cloudlets with a central cloud. The study analyzes performance metrics, including average waiting time, response time, and system utilization, under both configurations. Simulation results indicate that integrating cloudlets and clouds into a heterogeneous cloud significantly improves overall transcoding performance.

A cycle total edge colouring of a graph $G$ is defined as a proper edge colouring where each colour appears an even number of times within every cycle of $G$. It is established that every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta$ admits such a cycle total colouring using $\max\{4\Delta, \chi(G)+\Delta-1\}$ colours. This paper demonstrates an improved upper bound of $\max\{2\Delta+2, \chi(G)+\Delta-1\}$ for graphs $G$ satisfying $\Delta \geq 2$ and excluding those that are either bipartite, 3-connected, or isomorphic to $K_4$. Additionally, we prove that for any graph $G$ with $\Delta \geq 2$ and girth $g \geq 5$, a cycle total colouring exists using $\max\{3\Delta+2, \chi(G)+\Delta-1\}$ colours. Finally, we conjecture that a cycle total colouring with $\max\{4\Delta+2, \chi(G)+\Delta-1\}$ colours is feasible for all graphs with $\Delta \geq 2$.

This work analyzes the semi-classical dynamics of the energy supercritical Gross--Pitaevskii equation, defined by the parameter $\gamma > 1 + \frac{d}{2}$. We establish that the base state $Q_\epsilon$ possesses Morse index 1 in the energy functional constrained to the momentum and mass manifolds. Furthermore, utilizing this finding, we demonstrate that nodal vortices emerge in the semi-classical regime with high probability.

The regulatory landscape for evaluating new drug combinations with existing treatments is expanding, necessitating a robust statistical framework to validate claims of no type I error. This paper outlines a specific design for confirmatory clinical trials aimed at demonstrating the safety and efficacy of novel drug combinations. It details the trial design, statistical analysis plan, and the corresponding sample size calculations required to meet Type I error control standards.

The metaverse, a persistent, immersive, and interconnected virtual ecosystem, demands advanced rendering techniques to support its vast user base. This paper introduces Distributed Combined Rendering (DHR), a novel framework designed for rendering metaverse environments. DHR integrates the geometry of multiple scenes into a single, unified structure, enabling remote rendering of virtual objects across a distributed network. By utilizing virtual reality head-mounted displays (HMDs) to capture the user's viewpoint, DHR streams the necessary portions of the combined scene to distributed rendering nodes. These nodes then project the rendered content back to the user's HMD. Consequently, DHR facilitates the creation of expansive, collaborative environments capable of delivering high-fidelity metaverse experiences.

Music information retrieval (MIR) has gained significant traction in recent years, with extensive research efforts directed toward analyzing orchestral music. However, the inherent complexity of this music often complicates the annotation and alignment processes, leading to significant discrepancies between different datasets. This study introduces a novel orchestral music performance evaluation method that specifically addresses annotation and alignment precision. We validated this approach using a dataset of orchestral music pieces annotated by two distinct experts. The results demonstrate that the proposed method offers a more accurate assessment of performance than traditional approaches, thereby serving as a promising tool for future advancements in MIR.

This study introduces a novel self-interference cancellation (SIC) strategy for full-duplex (FD) systems, leveraging multi-antenna techniques to achieve simultaneous uplink and downlink transmissions. The proposed approach utilizes a multi-antenna setup to mitigate self-interference while concurrently enhancing the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of the downlink transmission. Specifically, the system assigns a dedicated antenna array to the downlink and another to the uplink. The SIC process involves three distinct phases: first, the downlink transmit weights are optimized to suppress interference; second, the receive weights for the uplink are optimized to suppress both interference and noise; third, the downlink weights are re-optimized to maximize the SINR. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SIC method outperforms existing solutions in both downlink SINR and achievable uplink spectral efficiency.

Colloidal droplets, which are liquid droplets dispersed within a continuous solvent, are extensively utilized in various fields, including medicine, food science, and cosmetics. While their liquid nature makes them susceptible to deformation and invagination under external forces, this study investigates the solidification dynamics of such droplets. We demonstrate that as the droplets transition from a liquid to a rigid state, they undergo a specific bending and invagination process. This morphological change is driven by the coupling of two distinct mechanisms: the reduction in droplet volume and the increase in its elastic modulus. Furthermore, the research examines how these invaginated droplets respond to external forces and analyzes the factors influencing their deformation and recovery.

We present a novel method for detecting and mapping the distribution of cold gas within protoplanetary disks by analyzing the spatial relationship between scattered ultraviolet (UV) continuum and Lyman-alpha (Ly$\alpha$) emission. This technique relies on the fact that UV continuum serves as a reliable tracer of the total gas column density, whereas Ly$\alpha$ emission is strongly suppressed by resonant scattering in dense gas. Consequently, the ratio of scattered UV to Ly$\alpha$ light intensifies as the gas density rises. We applied this approach to the protoplanetary disks around the young stars HD 169142 and HD 141569, utilizing the Hubble Space Telescope's Cosmic Origins Spectrograph. Our results indicate that the HD 169142 disk contains a cold gas component with a mass of $0.01\,M_{\odot}$, while HD 141569 exhibits a more complex structure featuring two distinct cold gas components with masses of $0.01\,M_{\odot}$ and $0.001\,M_{\odot}$, respectively. These findings align with previous observations of cold gas in these systems, confirming the utility of our proposed method.

This study introduces a machine learning framework for millimeter-wave localization leveraging radio fingerprints and adaptive intelligent surfaces (IS). The system utilizes a 28 GHz dual-panel phased array IS to mitigate multipath effects and enhance signal strength. The proposed algorithm employs a two-stage training approach: initially, a supervised deep neural network (DNN) is trained to estimate the position of the user equipment (UE) based on received signal power from the dual panels. Subsequently, a supervised D-DNN is trained to predict the UE's location using received power from the panels and the phase difference of signals arriving at the UE from a single panel. Simulation results demonstrate that this two-stage method achieves a positioning root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.12 m with 100 training samples, representing a 50% reduction compared to the single-panel approach. Furthermore, the algorithm exhibits robustness against user mobility and UE orientation changes.

We investigate the impact of uniform magnetic fields on the quantum states of neutral particles possessing a non-zero electric dipole moment, focusing on the asymptotic behavior of these states in the presence of such fields. Our analysis reveals that the resulting low-energy, ground states exhibit a helical or twisted structure. We further examine how this phenomenon applies to various entities, ranging from molecules to ultracold atoms and atoms, and even baryons and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultracold atoms and atoms, and ultrac

The surge in electric vehicle (EV) adoption necessitates a substantial expansion of the charging infrastructure. This study offers a comprehensive analysis of the location, pricing, and market structure within this network. It examines the interplay between private and public stations, evaluating how their respective costs and pricing strategies influence market dynamics. The research highlights that while the charging grid is a vital public good, it is equally a private business opportunity. Consequently, the study identifies optimal locations for both network types and determines the ideal pricing structure to maximize market share and profitability.

This study examines a scenario where a committee must choose one winner from three candidates based on a two-tiered ranking system. Specifically, the panel first divides the three candidates into two groups, and the resulting "tied" set is then ranked by an independent tie-breaker to produce the final rankings. The paper analyzes the relationship between two key fairness criteria: majority rule (where the winner is selected by a strict majority) and weak majority (allowing selection by a weak majority). The authors demonstrate that every voting rule satisfying both properties aligns with one of three structural types: (1) a tie-breaker ranking the candidate first by a single voter, (2) a tie-breaker ranking the candidate first by two voters, or (3) a tie-breaker ranking the candidate first by two voters, and the remaining candidate is selected by a single voter. The study further establishes that every voting rule satisfying both properties can be represented by a specific set of "minimal" rules, and that the "majority" rule is the only rule that maximizes the probability of selecting a winner with the highest average score.

This study investigates three-point correlation functions within ${\mathcal N}=1$ superconformal quantum field theories, specifically focusing on higher-spin spinor current multiplets. We derive general formulas for these three-point correlations and demonstrate that they are entirely determined by a single complex coupling constant, $c$, which serves as a complexification of the well-known $c_{SCFC}$ constant found in the corresponding three-point function of bosonic higher-spin currents. Furthermore, we establish the relationship between this coupling constant $c$ and the central charge $Z$.

We introduce a study assessing the level of machine understanding among 10-13 year old children, alongside an assessment of their ability to identify educational resources suitable for this demographic. The project involved administering a machine instruction quiz to 120 participants, followed by a survey of 86 individuals to determine their resource preferences, and a detailed examination of 23 resources to gauge the educational materials' appeal to the target audience. The findings indicate that most young learners possess limited machine instruction comprehension, with only 13.6% of the group achieving a passing score on the test. The preferred materials selected by the participants were largely unsuitable for teaching machine concepts to youth, as they were either too complex or entirely inappropriate. Conversely, the most engaging resources for the children were either non-interactive or failed to address machine instructions. The study concludes by offering recommendations for developing effective, age-appropriate machine instruction learning materials.

Reinforcement learning (RL) has garnered significant interest within both academic and industrial sectors, particularly in the context of robotics and gaming. However, the field is currently grappling with a critical challenge: the lack of robustness in existing RL algorithms. This fragility stems from the fact that these algorithms are highly sensitive to variations in the environment, such as changes in the reward function or the transition probability distribution. This paper reviews current research on RL, with a specific focus on two primary objectives: first, to examine how different algorithms perform under diverse environmental conditions; and second, to explore the integration of human knowledge into the learning process. To achieve these goals, we propose a unified framework for RL algorithms and evaluate their effectiveness across various environments. Our findings indicate that while current algorithms are effective in specific contexts, they often fail to generalize across others. To address this limitation, we suggest a novel approach that leverages human knowledge to enhance algorithmic performance.

We present a versatile, on-chip approach for controlling various onsets of light within the quantum domain. This method employs a single integrated photonic chip featuring a programmable mesh of directional couplers, driven by coherent classical signals across multiple dimensions of control—specifically polarization, spatial mode, and wavelength. This configuration facilitates the dynamic reconfiguration of quantum signal transformations across distinct degrees of freedom. We demonstrate its application in realizing entanglement between polarization and spatial modes, alongside the generation of four-mode entanglement utilizing polarization, spatial modes, and orbital angular momentum. These findings establish a robust foundation for the integrated control of light in quantum information processing and quantum communication systems.

This study investigates quantum conduction within DNA sequences featuring mismatches, employing a tight-binding model that incorporates quantum tunneling and electron-phonon interactions. We demonstrate that quantum tunneling, arising from quantum coherence, significantly enhances electron mobility. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that quantum fluctuations, driven by electron-phonon coupling, substantially influence conductance. These findings offer fresh perspectives on the role of quantum mechanics in biological systems.

This study addresses finding a resilient alignment for two point sets derived from different noisy observations of a shared 3D object. The proposed method iteratively refines the alignment using a K-means clustering strategy. Specifically, the process alternates between assigning points to clusters based on their current alignment and re-evaluating the alignment by considering only pairs of points from distinct clusters. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this approach guarantees convergence to a local optimum. Furthermore, the method exhibits robustness against outliers, as it relies solely on pairs from different clusters, and the effectiveness of this strategy is demonstrated through experiments on noisy 3D scans of real-world objects.

Tb$_3$Ru$_2$O$_7$ is a rare-earth oxide characterized by a unique crystal structure, where Ru atoms form chains with alternating bond lengths. This system exhibits a spin-3/2 magnetic moment, while the inequivalent Ru atoms experience distinct internal magnetic fields. This research investigates the magnetic ordering of Tb$_3$Ru$_2$O$_7$ using neutron powder diffraction and magnetic susceptibility. The findings reveal that Tb$^{3+}$ ions undergo a spin-ordered antiferromagnetic phase below $T_N = 10.5$ K, whereas the Ru$^{3+}$ moments remain disordered. The magnetic field generated by the ordered Tb$^{3+}$ ions is insufficient to induce ordering in the spin-3/2 Ru$^{3+}$ moments, despite the presence of alternating bond lengths. Consequently, the magnetic properties of Tb$_3$Ru$_2$O$_7$ are dominated by Tb$^{3+}$ ions, with the disordered Ru$^{3+}$ moments remaining unperturbed.

This paper explores mathematical optimization problems characterized by a difference of concave (DC) structure in their objective functions, with constraints defined by general equalities and inequalities. By utilizing DC approximation techniques, DC restricted mathematical optimization problems are formulated. The study presents several DC restricted optimization problems, alongside their corresponding Lagrangian and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Furthermore, the paper establishes KKT sufficiency and necessary optimality criteria for these restricted problems, while also demonstrating the relationship between DC programming and standard nonlinear programming.

We investigate the type IIB supergravity solution featuring a stack of D(-)-D(7) branes, with a specific focus on the geometry of the emergent string worldvolume. This setup is of interest because it offers a string-theoretic realization of the $AdS_1/SU(2)_k$ correspondence, where the $AdS_1$ space is defined by a constant dilaton and a linearly varying axion. We demonstrate that the near-horizon geometry of this brane configuration precisely matches the target $AdS_1/$CFT$0$ scenario. Furthermore, we analyze the spectrum of fluctuations around this background, identifying a set of modes that align with the lowest $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ multiplets in the $AdS_1/SU(2)$ theory. We also explore the implications of this framework for the $AdS_1/SU(2)$ duality, particularly concerning the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry and the behavior of fluctuation modes.

We present the concept of "area collision," which involves constructing new collision models in the plane by replacing standard Euclidean distance with an area metric derived from a Riemannian metric. We examine conditions under which the fundamental properties of three-dimensional collision—such as conservation of momentum and mass, minimization of total kinetic energy, and invariance under Möbius transformations remain valid. Furthermore, we apply these "area collision" models to submanifolds within spherical and hyperbolic 3-spaces, as well as to hypersurfaces within 4-dimensional Minkowski space.

This paper introduces a new framework designed to enhance learning efficiency in reinforcement learning (RL) for robotic control by embedding controller knowledge into the initial policy. The approach employs a Bayesian controller that synthesizes a weighted combination of a specialized controller and a generic base policy. This hybrid architecture enables the system to leverage established control strategies while simultaneously learning new behaviors. We validate the method across two distinct scenarios: a simulation-based bipedal walking task and a real-world robotic arm manipulation task. The results demonstrate that this integration accelerates learning compared to standard RL methods and offers robustness against noisy reward signals. Furthermore, the framework supports the transfer of policies across different robots, successfully adapting a policy trained on one robot to control another.

The perfusion analysis of cerebral blood flow (CBF) images is critical for diagnosing stroke and determining treatment strategies. However, the inherent low resolution of CBF images, resulting from the convolution of the original data with a point spread function (PSF), complicates the extraction of perfusion metrics. To address this, we introduce a differentiable deconvolution method that utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to reverse the convolution process. By rendering the operation differentiable, we can apply gradient-based optimization techniques to fine-tune the PSF parameters. This approach allows for the refinement of the PSF to better reflect the specific imaging conditions of the dataset. We evaluated the method using both synthetic and clinical data, comparing it against standard CBF perfusion analysis. Results indicate that this technique enhances stroke perfusion assessment by improving the accuracy of perfusion metrics.

We present the first calculation of the N$^3$LO zero-jettiness ray functions applicable to any massless 2-parton hard process at N$^3$LO. This achievement relies on a novel, efficient method for deriving the N$^3$LO factorized cross section, which utilizes the inherent symmetries of the renormalization group to bypass the traditional requirement of computing the complete N$^3LO factorized contribution.

This study examines the properties of the prime power graph within finite groups. We demonstrate that the graph is chordal if and only if it belongs to a specific small collection of groups, and we provide characterizations for both cases where it is chordal and where it is not chordal. Additionally, we analyze induced subgraphs of the power graph and investigate its planarity. We prove that power graphs are planar only for a limited set of groups, and we offer simplified necessary conditions for planarity in finite abelian and $p$-groups. Finally, we establish that the power graph of a finite group is chordal precisely when it is abelian, symmetric ($S_3$), or the Dickson group ($D_{2n}$).

This study addresses the challenge of isolating a specific source within a noisy mixture. We introduce a new deep neural network designed to extract a target source from such mixtures, leveraging training data consisting of the target source alongside background noise. Our methodology relies on a dedicated network that learns to reconstruct the target source from the input mixture and reference noise. We further propose an optimal domain adaptation strategy to bridge the disparity between training and test conditions regarding noise characteristics. This approach involves training on environments populated with known noise types and then testing in environments featuring novel, unseen noise types. Our experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

The concept of quantum coherence is crucial for understanding quantum phenomena, yet it is typically defined based on specific, often arbitrary, decompositions of Hilbert space. This work proposes a more general framework for identifying coherence within universal quantum observations, a concept that is decomposition-independent and instead relies on a Hilbert space structure derived from the system's density matrix. We demonstrate that this coherence measure is invariant under unitary transformations and provides a decomposition-independent metric for the distinctiveness of quantum states. We also discuss the implications of our findings for various areas, including quantum thermodynamics and the study of quantum correlations.

We present a study of Type C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the black hole X-ray binary H 1743-322, utilizing data from the 2012-2013 outbursts recorded by the NICER and NuSTAR space observatories. Our analysis reveals that the QPO frequency remains stable within a single outburst, fluctuating by approximately 10% in the 2012 campaign and 15% in the 2013 campaign. By correlating these findings with the known relationship between QPO frequency and black hole spin, we infer that the spin parameter is roughly 0.9, indicating that H 1743-322 is a high-spin stellar-mass black hole. Furthermore, we observe that the QPO frequency correlates with the X-ray luminosity, a relationship that can be explained by the QPO frequency serving as a proxy for the inner accretion disk radius. This correlation implies that the inner accretion disk radius varies by a factor of 2-3 across different outburst phases. Additionally, we identify a novel QPO frequency of 1.25 Hz in the 2013 outburst, which is significantly lower than the 2.5 Hz frequency detected in 2012. The paper introduces a novel framework designed for the automated creation of legal documents, specifically targeting the reduction of bureaucratic delays and associated costs. This system is grounded in a question-answading architecture that leverages a specialized, domain-specific pre-trained language model. The model was developed using a dataset of 100,000 questions paired with their official legal responses, covering various aspects of Indian law. Our approach utilizes a robust pipeline comprising a QnA detector, a sentence transformer for retrieval, and a decoder for answering. The system achieves a precision-recall F1 score of 0.81 and an ROC-AUC of 0.85. Additionally, we have made the system's code and pre-trained model publicly accessible.

The missing baryon problem, a significant challenge in cosmology, involves identifying the location of the remaining baryons that exceed the count of dark matter. While the majority of baryons are expected to reside within the Milky Way's halo, the precise location of these baryons remains uncertain. This study utilizes the EAGLE cosmological hydrodynamic simulation suite to investigate the distribution of baryons in the Milky Way's vicinity. We identify that the EAGLE simulation's Milky Way is characterized by a stellar mass of $10^{11} M_{\odot}$, a halo mass of $10^{12} M_{\odot}$, and a distance of 8 Mpc from the center of the Milky Way. We find that the EAGLE simulation is consistent with the observed baryon density in the Milky Way's vicinity, which is approximately $10^{-3} M_{\odot}/Mpc^3$. A sequence divider is defined as a contiguous subsequence within a sequence that does not appear as a contiguous subsequence anywhere earlier in the sequence. We introduce an algorithm designed to identify all leftmost sequence dividers of size $k$ or less in a given sequence of size $n$, operating with a time complexity of $O(n \log n)$ and a space requirement of $O(n/k \log n)$.

We present findings from a systematic search for transient events within a sample of 100 post-starburst and dormant Balmer-strong galaxies. This sample, drawn from the SDSS DR10, was selected based on specific criteria: a $g-r$ color greater than 0.1, a $g-r$ color gradient exceeding 0.02 mag/kpc, and a Balmer absorption line index above 0.1. The search utilized the ZTF Transient Server, which covers the full SDSS footprint, to identify transient events with peak magnitudes brighter than $g=20.5$ mag. We detected 11 transient events, comprising 7 Type Ia supernovae, 3 Type II supernovae, and 1 Type IIn supernova. The Type Ia events are distributed across the sample with 6 events in post-starburst galaxies and 1 in a dormant Balmer-strong galaxy, while the Type II events are found in 2 post-starburst galaxies and 1 in a dormant Balmer-strong galaxy. The Type IIn event is located in a post-starburst galaxy. We calculated the expected detection rates for Type Ia supernovae and Type II supernovae based on the local star formation rate history and the star formation history of the sample, respectively. Reconfigurable Wireless Networks (RWNs) are emerging as a promising solution for next-generation wireless systems, offering superior flexibility and performance. However, the challenge of efficiently allocating resources in these networks is significantly more complex than in traditional ones, primarily due to the vast number of potential reconfiguration options. This study addresses this issue by introducing a novel QoS-aware scheduler for RWNs that leverages the synergy between reinforcement learning (RL) and inverse reinforcement learning (IRL). In this proposed framework, a Performer-Critic model serves as the learning agent, while the inverse reinforcement method is utilized to derive reward signals. By integrating these components, the approach effectively mitigates the high computational costs associated with training deep RL models in RWNs. The research further demonstrates that the performance of the proposed Performer-Critic architecture surpasses that of standard Performer models.

Current term-level assessment methods for post-editing support are constrained by their reliance on pre-defined quality criteria, which often fail to adequately cover the complexities of post-editing decisions. Consequently, we introduce a new framework that integrates a quality dimension into a rule-based scoring system, allowing for the adaptive prioritization of different quality aspects during the post-editing process. This approach is validated through a crowdsourced experiment, which demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms existing models.

We investigate the shadows of Kerr--de Sitter dark stars within the context of the Einstein--Maxwell--Ashtekar--Baez--Strominger theory, which posits a cosmological constant $\Lambda$ as a quantum number. Specifically, we examine the possibility of determining the value of this constant by analyzing the shadows of such objects. Our findings indicate that the shadow radius of a Kerr--de Sitter dark star is highly sensitive to $\Lambda$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the shadow radius varies linearly with $\Lambda$ for a fixed mass and spin, and that the magnitude of this variation increases with the object's mass. Additionally, we show that the shadow radius of a Kerr--de Sitter dark star is greater than that of a Kerr black hole, and that the shadow radius of a Schwarzschild black hole exceeds that of a Schwarzschild--de Sitter black hole. These results suggest that the shadow radius of a black hole is a useful probe of the value of the cosmological constant.

This work introduces a novel framework for solving the relativistic fluid dynamics equations in two-dimensional Cartesian space, designed to facilitate the numerical investigation of relativistic hydrodynamics. The approach employs a new method for decomposing the four-velocity and four-current vectors, which are expressed as linear combinations of the four equations. This formulation is applied to the continuity equation, energy-momentum conservation, and particle transport, enabling the derivation of an explicit system of equations in a 2D Cartesian grid. The resulting system is solved using a standard Runge-Kutta method, with results benchmarked against the well-known 2D Riemann problem. The work concludes with a discussion of the method's advantages and potential limitations.

This study examines the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ mesons, which decay into $D^{*+} K^0_{\rm S}$ and $D^{*0} K^+$ final states, utilizing the LHCb dataset of $1.0\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s}=7\,\text{TeV}$. The analysis identifies a single candidate for the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ meson, designated as $D^{(*)+}_{s1}$, with a mass of $2612.00 \pm 0.05\,\text{MeV}/c^2$ and a width of $1.90 \pm 0.05\,\text{MeV}$. These findings align with the established properties of the $D^{(*)+}_{s1}(2536)$ meson.

This paper introduces a novel class of fractal polynomials defined on the Sierpiński gasket and investigates their fundamental properties. The work establishes the existence of a homomorphism linking the polynomials of continuous functions on the gasket to a specific algebra of complex polynomials. The proof leverages the wavelet decomposition of function spaces on the gasket, alongside the construction of fractal polynomials and wavelets grounded in a B-spline scaling function. Furthermore, the study examines approximation capabilities, interpolation techniques, and the equicontinuity of these fractal polynomials. Finally, it explores generalized fractal polynomials across various self-similar sets and analyzes their connections to fractal functions and wavelets.

We introduce a novel approach to facilitating visual exploration through the integration of natural language queries with image databases. This system utilizes a question-answering component to interpret text inputs, which then converts user queries into precise search criteria for the database. By providing accurate answers to follow-up questions, the system further refines the query logic, enabling the directed exploration of large-scale image collections. Our methodology is designed to be adaptable across various domains, including visual object detection, segmentation, and image retrieval.

The cusp-core theorem posits that dark matter (DM) halos with gaseous, dissipative central components will inherently evolve into a low-density, core-like structure. This study examines whether supernova (SN) explosions serve as a mechanism for transforming steep DM cusps into cores within dwarf galaxies, utilizing the analytic framework proposed by \citet{Sigurdsson1996}. We demonstrate that the validity of this method relies on the assumption that the DM density profile remains unchanged during the SN feedback process. However, we argue that this assumption is flawed because the energy injected by the SN feedback inevitably alters the DM density distribution. Consequently, the current analytical approach cannot accurately quantify the core size generated by SN feedback. Furthermore, we contend that the SN feedback mechanism is insufficient to account for the cores observed in dwarf galaxies.

This study examines how to minimize the size of first-order formulae derived from higher-order logic proofs, a task that is crucial for enhancing the performance of automated theorem provers. We introduce a novel extraction method tailored to a SAT-based two-phase solving strategy, which leverages higher-order one-model-based (HO1) semantics by extracting information from arbitrary valid assignments. We detail the methodology and present preliminary experimental results.

This study examines how transforming the right-hand side of replicator equations influences their long-term dynamics. We demonstrate that specific, structurally straightforward transformations result in replicator equations that maintain a stable equilibrium and possess a trajectory that converges to this same stable point.

This paper establishes the asymptotic normality of multivariate random forest estimators, extending existing literature that primarily addresses univariate asymptotic properties. We demonstrate the consistency of these estimators within a multivariate context and derive their asymptotic variance-covariance matrix, thereby enabling the construction of multivariate confidence intervals. The theoretical findings are supported by a simulation study designed to validate the derived asymptotic results.

This study addresses the challenge of scheduling electric vehicle (EV) charging within distribution grids characterized by asymmetrical voltage and three-phase configurations. The proposed solution leverages an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) framework, designed to minimize aggregate charging costs while adhering to grid constraints. To mitigate the high communication overhead inherent in ADMM, we implement a communication-restricted strategy that restricts exchanges to only those phases and buses directly impacted by recent updates. We further analyze the algorithm's convergence properties, accounting for the reduced communication scope, and substantiate these findings with numerical experiments.

The structural, electronic, and elastic properties of orthorhombic SmFeO$_3$ were investigated using the density functional theory (DFT) within the generalized gradient approximation (GGA). The study employed three distinct functionals: the Perdew-Burk-Ernzerhof (PBE) GGA, the modified Becke-Johnson (mBJ) potential, and the HSE06 hybrid functional. Structural parameters derived from these methods were compared against experimental data, revealing that the PBE GGA yields the closest agreement. Furthermore, the mBJ potential was found to be superior to the PBE GGA in describing the material's electronic structure.

The gut microbiome is a complex ecosystem of bacteria, archaea, viruses, and fungi that resides within the human digestive tract. Although its specific functions remain partially unknown, it is clear that the microbiome plays a critical role in human health. This study introduces a computational framework designed to analyze the functional dynamics of the gut microbiome. By integrating metagenomic data with metabolic models, we developed a method to construct genome-scale metabolic reconstructions for thousands of microbial genomes. This approach enables the investigation of individual microbial species' metabolic capabilities as well as their collective community functions. Furthermore, we applied this methodology to a human gut microbiome dataset, generating 100,000 metabolic models to elucidate the metabolic pathways of the gut microbiome. Our analysis revealed that the microbiome harbors a vast array of nutrients and metabolites, including amino acids, vitamins, and short-chain fatty acids. Additionally, we identified key metabolic pathways that are essential for the community's survival and function. Overall, this study demonstrates the utility of computational methods in deciphering the intricate metabolic networks of the gut microbiome.

This study introduces a data-driven modeling approach for ventilating intelligent building systems, leveraging the growing availability of high-frequency data from IoT sensors. The proposed methodology integrates data exploration, feature engineering, and supervised learning to construct a data model that captures the system's operational dynamics. The model's performance was validated using data from a real-world case study, with results demonstrating that this approach is both effective and practical for such applications.

We present the discovery of a new superluminous supernova, SN 2017gci, located in the nearby galaxy NGC 4490+NGC 4491. This object is identified as a Type I, hydrogen-deficient superluminous supernova (SLSN-I), characterized by a peak absolute magnitude of $M_{\rm max} = -21.1$ mag and a peak bolometric luminosity of $2.5 \times 10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$. Its light curve exhibits a slow rise, a broad profile, and a long duration, with a total duration of $t_{\rm 90} = 190$ days. The spectral evolution shows a distinct blueward shift in the Balmer series absorption lines over time. We propose that SN 2017gci results from the merger of a white dwarf and a helium star. This scenario is supported by the object's high bolometric luminosity, broad spectral features, and blueward spectral shifts, all of which are consistent with the interaction of a merger ejecta shell with a helium star's dense envelope.

We present a quantum mechanical framework describing the magnetization reversal of two-dimensional solitary domain magnets. This approach incorporates both the intrinsic and extrinsic influences of spin-orbit coupling, which are critical for the Stoner-Wohlfarth mechanism. The resulting theory predicts that the first-order reversal curve (FRC) exhibits a distinct dependence on the magnitude of quantum spin fluctuations. These fluctuations are governed by the quantum parameter, which is determined by the ratio of the zero-point energy to the thermal energy. The theoretical predictions align well with recent experimental findings.

While current methods typically rely on a two-stage process involving object detection followed by dependency prediction, they often suffer from a lack of global context, resulting in incomplete dependency structures. To address this, we introduce a novel framework that integrates object detection with a new approach to visual perception. This method utilizes a novel "visual attention" mechanism to capture global contextual information, thereby enhancing the accuracy of detecting object dependencies. Feature contribution techniques are widely employed to interpret machine learning models, yet most existing methods operate within the image's pixel space, often neglecting model performance directly in the picture domain. This study introduces a new approach that shifts assessment from pixel space to picture space by integrating a simple pre-processing step that maps pixels into picture representations. We then extend a standard feature attribution method to this new picture representation, allowing for the calculation of picture-level contributions. We demonstrate that this method enables the direct identification of influential pictures and their specific regions, offering a fresh perspective for interpretability. Additionally, we show that these picture-level contributions align with traditional pixel-space analyses, thereby preserving the original method's interpretative benefits.

This study investigates the linearization stability of thin-shell wormholes constructed from a general static, spherically symmetric spacetime, where the gravitational source is not symmetric across the reflecting surface. We demonstrate that the conditions required for linearization stability are independent of the presence of reflective boundaries. Furthermore, we analyze the wormhole's causal structure, revealing the existence of dual shadows when the source is not globally spherically symmetric. We further establish that a causal path connecting the two wormhole mouths may exist, depending on the source configuration.

This paper outlines the current state of research on the trimer shield problem defined on the triangular lattice. In this configuration, trimer covers are placed on the lattice's edges to prevent any adjacent empty sites from appearing. Although certain exact solutions exist for specific lattice variants, the triangular case remains unsolved. The primary difficulty stems from the fact that valid configurations are represented by a complex set of interacting local rules, which complicates the application of standard statistical mechanics techniques. Consequently, this study examines the problem's fundamental characteristics, including its phase transitions, height function behavior, and universal scaling properties, while also addressing the challenges of defining and calculating the density of unshielded edges.

This study tackles the challenge of universal domain adaptation, which involves sequentially adapting a series of source domains to a single target domain. While existing universal adaptation methods typically rely on learning a shared representation to align multiple source domains with the target, they often overlook the critical insight that source domains and the target are connected through specific exemplars. Consequently, we introduce a novel framework that learns classifiers based on prototypes and mutual point instances to achieve universal domain adaptation. Specifically, we develop a Prototypical Classifier utilizing mutual point learning to align source domains with the target, and we further implement a Mutual Point Classifier to facilitate sequential domain adaptation. Experimental evaluations on six datasets confirm the proposed method's effectiveness and superiority over state-of-the-art approaches.

This study introduces a novel method for assessing the 3D poses of vehicles from stereo imagery and reconstructing their shapes. Unlike existing approaches that rely on vehicle-free priors, our technique leverages specific shape characteristics of different car categories. We begin by constructing a library of 3D models for various vehicle types, followed by the creation of a pose evaluation metric that integrates the likelihood of a pose given the image and a high prior probability of a given vehicle type. Subsequently, a shape recovery process is executed by maximizing the posterior probability of the vehicle's 3D shape given the pose and the visual input. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves higher precision in both pose estimation and shape reconstruction compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

Querying knowledge graphs (KGs) using natural language is a critical area of research, yet constructing the necessary query structure remains a significant hurdle. While prior methods have addressed KG completion by predicting missing facts, they often overlook the essential step of outlining the entire query schema. This paper introduces a novel hierarchical framework for generating such structures, designed to manage complex natural language questions. Our approach decomposes intricate queries into manageable sub-components, enabling a more systematic and organized query process. We validate this method through comprehensive experiments on the WebQSP benchmark, where our model outperforms state-of-the-art techniques by 10.5% in exact match accuracy and 15.3% in coreference accuracy.

This study introduces a novel algebraic structure, termed a "monoid space," which serves as a unifying framework for diverse mathematical domains, ranging from algebraic equations to specific differential systems. The concept relies on the interaction between a monoid and a vector space, where the monoid's elements act as linear transformations. We demonstrate that this framework encompasses various mathematical theories, including the algebraic formulation of polynomial equations, the theory of linear difference equations, and the theory of linear scalar difference equations. The paper further explores the connections among these theories and their applications, specifically examining the role of monoid spaces in the context of the "differential algebra of polynomials."

The surge in data volume and the need for its rapid processing have led to the adoption of streaming graphs, which offer a more efficient alternative to traditional graph structures. In this paper, we present a benchmark evaluating various named entity resolution techniques specifically for streaming graphs. We examine multiple algorithms, including rule-based approaches, similarity measures, and machine learning methods. Our findings indicate that machine learning approaches are particularly effective for this task, provided that the corresponding models are trained on high-quality data.

This paper addresses one-loop corrections to the scalar mass matrices within the MSSM, incorporating effects from all Yukawa couplings. We derive the corrections to the scalar top and bottom sectors, presenting the results in a diagonal basis. We also examine the trace and traceless parts of these corrections, demonstrating that the traceless elements are proportional to the Yukawa couplings. We begin by deriving the corrections to the scalar top and bottom matrices, presenting them in a basis where they are already partially diagonal. We introduce a new approach for automatically generating dynamic camera perspectives from footage captured by a single camera. This system utilizes a deep learning model to identify salient objects and their features, estimating their 3D positions and the object's pose. It then employs a deep learning model to synthesize a dynamic viewpoint by leveraging camera trajectory, object 3D data, and the object's appearance. We have developed a novel dataset comprising 3D object reconstructions and dynamic viewpoint sequences captured from a single 2D image to support this task. Experimental results demonstrate that our method successfully generates dynamic viewpoints of objects in real-world scenes from a single 2D image.

This paper examines the existence of bounded prior solutions for coarse differential equations incorporating a non-linear damping term. These equations serve as approximations to ordinary differential equations (ODs) and arise from applying the coarsening method to ODEs. The authors establish the existence of such limits for a specific class of coarse equations featuring a non-linear damping term, which generalizes a prior study focused on linear damping terms. The analysis relies on the existence of solutions to associated boundary value problems.

We demonstrate that for the random grain model, the scaling factor for nonlinear statistics scales as $N^{1/3}$, where $N$ represents the count of constituent grains. This finding holds true across various statistical measures, including the maximum, the second-largest component, and the boundary of the convex hull. We further extend the analysis to nonlinear quantities of the grains' boundaries themselves. Within the context of the Burgers' equation, these findings indicate that the amplitude of the shock front scales as $t^{-1/3}$, where $t$ denotes time, and that the wave profile's spatial width contracts according to $t^{1/3}$.

Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are emerging as a promising technology for next-generation wireless systems. RISs consist of vast arrays of low-cost, energy-efficient, and compact elements that can be managed to manipulate electromagnetic waves. This paper examines the fundamental principles of RISs and their potential to enable the deployment of large-scale, energy-efficient, and flexible intelligent networks. We review the primary applications of RISs, including enhanced connectivity, elevated spectral efficiency, improved energy savings, and reduced carbon emissions. Furthermore, we identify critical hurdles in realizing RIS-based sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks, such as scalability, signal propagation, hardware imperfections, and the need for robust control mechanisms. Finally, we outline future research directions aimed at overcoming these obstacles and realizing the full promise of RIS technology.

We introduce a coarse-graining technique for multi-agent probabilistic systems characterized by multiple stable regions, enabling the derivation of a reduced effective model that retains the original system's key dynamical traits. This approach relies on a generalised form of the Fokker-Planck equation, which is valid under conditions of weak noise and slowly varying parameters. By integrating this equation with a specific coarse-graining procedure, we can eliminate fast time-scale dynamics and irrelevant spatial details, focusing instead on the essential areas of multistability. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method by applying it to a model of interacting agents where the coarse-grained potential landscape is governed by a single control parameter. In this simplified model, the relative positions of stable areas are preserved, and the connections between these regions are defined by transition rates that accurately reflect those of the original system.

Quantization is a primary strategy for reducing the memory footprint of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to facilitate deployment on resource-constrained devices. Although this technique lowers memory usage, it often results in a decline in model accuracy. This paper introduces a cyclic training approach that alternates between quantized and floating-point phases to enhance the convergence of quantized models. By utilizing a floating-point network as a reference, the method prevents performance degradation associated with quantization. We demonstrate that this technique is highly effective across various quantization stages, enabling the creation of lightweight models that maintain high accuracy. Our experimental results show that cyclic training can achieve up to 1.5% higher accuracy than standard quantization across three distinct architectures.

We introduce a novel class of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) that originate from the merger of two white dwarfs (WDs) with a combined mass slightly exceeding the Chandrasekhar limit ($M_{\rm Ch}$). These events, termed "near-$M_{\rm Ch}$" SNe Ia, are characterized by a distinct lack of hydrogen and helium lines alongside a low-velocity Ca II absorption feature. Their light curves exhibit a notably slow rise and decline, with peak luminosities approximately 0.5 magnitudes fainter than those of standard SNe Ia. We demonstrate that WD mergers occurring in dense stellar environments—such as globular clusters and the galactic bulges—can account for a substantial portion of the observed SN Ia population. By analyzing the available observational data, we estimate that roughly 10% of all SNe Ia arise from WD mergers in these environments. Consequently, the resulting near-$M_{\rm Ch}$ SNe Ia are expected to be significantly more common than the standard events, potentially comprising 30% to 50% of all SNe Ia.

The paper introduces a conceptual framework for analyzing the macro-structure of education, referred to as "everytime education at the macro scale," and explores its relationship with traditional educational macroeconomics. It is argued that, within this "whenever education" perspective, the educational process is viewed as a continuous, inherent, and ubiquitous state rather than a discrete economic activity. Consequently, this perspective reframes educational outcomes as a non-quantifiable, qualitative attribute, shifting the focus from the temporal duration of education to its pervasive nature.

Addressing the global pandemic of Covid-19 requires the development of robust, scalable, and interoperable digital systems. Blockchain technology offers a secure and efficient framework for data exchange, making it a viable solution for managing Covid-19 outbreaks. This study introduces a new blockchain-based architecture designed to facilitate vaccine distribution and administration during the pandemic. The proposed system leverages blockchain to ensure data integrity, security, and auditability, thereby establishing a reliable and transparent mechanism for vaccine tracking.

Course clustering involves organizing vast collections of course data into meaningful groups. While clustering algorithms are ubiquitous in data mining, their application to education has been limited, with prior research primarily focusing on evaluating the quality of individual course clusters rather than the clusters themselves. This study introduces a novel approach to analyzing course clusters by drawing parallels between clusters and social network communities. By applying community detection algorithms to cluster clusters, we uncover hidden patterns within educational data. Our findings demonstrate that this method effectively identifies specific course clusters, elucidates the characteristics of these subgroups, and offers valuable insights for higher education institutions.

We investigate the mechanism of localization within a one-dimensional periodic system of alternating chains composed of fermions and antifermions, which are coupled via a weak interaction. In the absence of this coupling, the system exhibits an insulating state characterized by a band gap. We demonstrate that even a minimal inter-chain interaction induces a phase transition into a conducting phase, marked by the emergence of localized mid-gap states. This transition is driven by the breaking of particle-antiparticle symmetry, resulting in a significant amplification of the energy gap between those symmetric and symmetrically broken bands. Consequently, the energy gap for the broken-symmetry mid-gap states scales inversely with the square of the interaction strength, specifically proportional to $1/U^2$.

This study examines the damping of spin waves within a two-dimensional, highly magnetized electron plasma, where spin-spin interactions are negligible and damping arises solely from hyperfine interactions with background nuclei. The analysis reveals that the damping rate for the fundamental spin precession mode is independent of wave number, whereas the rate for the first excited mode exhibits a linear dependence on wave number. Furthermore, the theoretical expressions for these damping rates are derived and validated against numerical simulations.

This study examines a conformal Floquet system driven by a continuous protocol, where the Floquet Hamiltonian itself undergoes a smooth temporal evolution. We demonstrate that a conformal symmetry links the evolution of the Floquet Hamiltonian with that of an energy-dependent one, a relationship that remains invariant under gauge transformations. Leveraging this conformal symmetry, we derive the exact analytical forms for the Floquet Hamiltonian and the corresponding unitary operator. Furthermore, we investigate the Berry curvature associated with the Floquet Hamiltonian and determine its closed-form expression.

This paper introduces a new approach to multimodal learning that overcomes the limitations of traditional methods by addressing the difficulty of integrating diverse data types. While existing techniques typically concatenate features across modalities, they often fail to account for the unique characteristics of each modality, resulting in suboptimal performance. Our proposed solution constructs a unified latent representation space for all modalities, enabling the fusion of features that retains their individual traits. We validate this method through experiments on the challenging "Which-Of-What-Is-It?" dataset, demonstrating significant performance gains over existing state-of-the-art approaches.

The study presents a measurement of the time-dependent CP asymmetry in the decay of the $B_s^0 \to J/\psi\phi$ channel, yielding $\sin\phi_s = -0.04 \pm 0.12 \pm 0.08$, where the first error is statistical and the second systematic. Additionally, an analysis of the $B_s^0$ meson's lifetime difference is reported, with a value of $\Delta\Gamma_s = 0.07 \pm 0.06 \pm 0.05~\text{ps}^{-1}$ (statistical and systematic uncertainties respectively). These findings are derived from data collected by the LHCb detector during 2011 and 2012, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $1~\text{fb}^{-1}$.

This paper introduces a novel framework for distributedly managing network resources, where each connected node operates independently. The approach is designed to achieve optimal resource allocation, defined as a state where marginal utilities are equalized across all links. The management scheme is built upon a conceptual model of a "graph device," which represents an idealized, cost-free instrument that interacts with the entire network. This study introduces a labeled random finite collection (Labeled-RFS) origin sampler designed to integrate information from multiple sensors. The method begins by sampling origins from the posterior RFS using a simple mean-field origin sampler. Subsequently, an adaptive particle filter is employed to estimate the posterior origin distribution conditioned on the sampled points, thereby updating the origin of each particle with associated labels. This approach offers significant computational efficiency, as the particle filter's cost is a small fraction of that of a standard origin sampler. The filter is optimized by utilizing posterior information and by incorporating constraints derived from the support of the posterior origin sampler to minimize the number of particles required. Nevertheless, RL agents often require millions of interactions with the environment to learn, a process that can be prohibitively costly or ethically problematic in certain contexts. Off-policy evaluation (OPE) methods have been developed to estimate an RL policy's value by analyzing historical data collected by a different behavior policy, thereby eliminating the need for environment interactions. This study evaluates the performance of multiple OPE techniques, specifically focusing on importance sampling (IS), weighted importance sampling (WIS), and Q-learning-based approaches. We benchmark these methods using a range of environments, including those with low and high action spaces, and compare their results against the on-policy baseline. Our findings indicate that WIS and Q-learning-based methods consistently outperform IS across all tested scenarios. The energy-momentum link of a strongly interacting polaron, which is formed by an electron trapped in a self-generated polariton cloud, is derived using the polaron's mass renormalized energy-momentum vector. A distinctive feature of this equation of motion is that it functions as a parabolic equation. However, theoretical analysis indicates that this equation can only remain valid up to a specific maximum momentum, which is determined by the Fermi velocity of the underlying medium.

We investigate the force-free limit of holographic plasma situated within an electromagnetic environment, utilizing the force-free limit of the effective action to determine the resulting boundary. By examining the stability of this boundary, we identify the condition that ensures a finite lifespan for the associated operator. Our findings indicate that, unlike the standard force-free case, this lifespan is generally finite due to the induced modification of the effective action.

This discussion explores a quantum version of the duality principle first identified in mathematics by Euler and later central to string theory. We examine how this principle applies to both wavefunction and operator formalisms within quantum mechanics, as well as to the string theory S-duality. A key insight is that the phenomenon is best understood as a correspondence between two distinct descriptions of the same system, where one is the "primal" and the other is the "dual." We argue that the "primal" description corresponds to the formulation utilizing the most symmetrical set of covariant tools. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the "primal" wavefunction obeys a covariant Schrödinger equation, while the "primal" operator framework relies on covariant gauge theories.

We examine periodic mappings $f: X \to X$ on a metric space $X$ and establish a connection between the asymptotic behavior of their orbits and the properties of associated curves $\gamma: \mathbb{R} \to X$ that remain nonexpansive under a given metric. Specifically, we demonstrate that for any periodic map $f$ with period $p$, there exists a nonexpansive curve $\gamma$ defined on the entire real line such that $\gamma(t+p) = f(\gamma(t))$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$. We further analyze the relationship between the set of all such curves $\gamma$ and the set of all periodic mappings $f$ that share the same periodicity $p$.

This paper presents a novel method for determining the exact Gromov-Hausdorff distance between metric spaces, specifically designed for the case of two finite metric spaces. We demonstrate that the minimal size of the symmetric difference between the two spaces, required to achieve the Gromov-Hausdorff equivalence, must be even. We further prove that this minimal measure equals twice the Borsuk number of this symmetric difference. We define the Borsuk number for a general set as being equal to its diameter, provided the set's diameter exceeds one; otherwise, it is defined as one half of its cardinality. We conclude by showing how to calculate the exact Gromov-Hausdorff distance between two finite metric spaces by utilizing this concept of Borsuk's number.

This paper investigates fourth-order elliptic equations featuring rapidly oscillating first-order and zeroth-order coefficients. We establish homogenization limits for these equations in the resolvent forms $u = (\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon + \lambda)^{-1}f$ and $v = \mathcal{L}_\varepsilon^{-1}f$, where $\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon$ represents a fourth-order differential operator with oscillating coefficients defined on the torus. The analysis covers the case where $\lambda$ is a complex number with a positive imaginary part, as well as the scenario where $\lambda$ is a Dirichlet eigenvalue of the homogenized operator.

The ability to handle multiple languages is a critical requirement for modern dialogue systems. While current research predominantly prioritizes English, the field lacks comprehensive investigations into the multilingual capabilities of state-of-the-art task-oriented dialogue (TOD) architectures. This study examines how conversation history impacts the multilingual performance of two prominent frameworks: the API-driven ATIS system and the template-based TOD system. We assess these models using the ATIS 3 and ATIS 4 datasets, which cover English, French, German, and Spanish. Our findings indicate that conversation history significantly influences multilingual task dialogues, with performance gains in lower-resource languages being more pronounced than in high-resource ones. Furthermore, we demonstrate that while conversation history is vital for handling cross-lingual inputs, it can introduce noise in monolingual contexts.

We introduce Smt-Switch, a solver-independent interface designed to streamline the integration of solvers within C++ applications. Our primary objective is to eliminate the laborious and error-prone process of configuring individual SMT solver configurations. In addition to streamlining connections, Smt-Switch facilitates the exchange of data between the host application and solvers, including model extraction, while also offering capabilities to manage solver crashes. Our implementation supports both Z3 and CVC5, and we have evaluated its impact on runtime overhead, demonstrating that it remains negligible.

This study examines the sextic anharmonic and Bender-Dunne potentials within the quasi-precisely solvable context. We derive exact analytical expressions for the energy eigenvalues and corresponding wave functions of the Schrödinger equation, applicable to both scenarios. This success stems from employing a generalized form of the Polyanyan method, which incorporates a specific transformation of coordinates. Furthermore, we calculate the expectation values of the position and momentum operators, as well as the momentum variance, for the resulting system.

We introduce a new methodology for enhancing image clarity to boost the precision of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This approach is designed to work alongside existing image preprocessing techniques and requires no additional parameters or floating-point operations (FLOPS) within the CNN architecture itself. By utilizing a simple yet effective strategy, this method increases image clarity, which in turn improves the accuracy of the models. We evaluated the effectiveness of this technique on the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets using various CNN models. The results indicate that this method yields an accuracy gain of 0.8% to 1.0% on CIFAR-10 and 0.25% to 0.5% on ImageNet.

The DART mission successfully altered Dimorphos's orbit by colliding with it, thereby changing the system's barycenter. This study examines how Dimorphos's rotation rate evolved post-impact, specifically analyzing the spin-induced motion of surface boulders. We demonstrate that boulders can migrate several meters across the body due to the YORP effect, a phenomenon driven by solar radiation pressure. This movement is especially significant for Dimorphos because its orbital period is so short; even minor shifts in boulder location can influence the system's overall barycenter. To address this, we developed a novel method for calculating the YORP torque that accounts for surface topography. Applying this technique to a model of Dimorphos's topography, we estimated the magnitude of the YORP force and projected future surface evolution. Our results indicate that the YORP effect will continue to drive granular motion for many centuries, and that the cumulative shift in the barycenter resulting from these movements could persist for hundreds of years after the DART impact.

We investigate the stability of charged scalar field configurations in the vicinity of a Reissner-Nordstrom black hole, revealing that the lowest-lying states are stable. Conversely, higher-lying states exhibit instability, with the most unstable mode possessing a long duration. This finding contradicts the general consensus that black hole scalar hair is generally unstable. We further demonstrate that these specific low-lying modes satisfy the no-hair theorem proposed by Harada and Koyama, as well as the conjecture by Chamseddine, Herzberg, and Noui.

This study provides a quantitative evaluation of the minimal active-sterile neutrino framework, wherein sterile neutrinos couple to the Standard Model solely through mixing with muon neutrinos. By analyzing the projected sensitivity of the J-PARC experiment to sterile neutrinos at the GeV scale, we determine the constraints on mixing parameters $\sin^2 2\theta_{\mu N}$ and $\Delta m^2_{N}$ derived from the expected sterile neutrino disappearance. Our findings indicate that the projected sensitivity reaches $\sin^2 2\theta N \sim 10^{-3}$ for $\Delta m^2_{N} \sim 1$ eV$^2$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the minimal active-sterile neutrino model can be tested via the $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay of $^{136}$Xe, yielding a sensitivity of $\sin^2 2\theta N \sim 10^{-4}$ for $\Delta m^2_{N} \sim 1$ eV$^2$.

Real-world image denoising is a critical challenge in computer vision, yet existing approaches often fail to address the issue effectively. This paper introduces a novel self-supervised denoising framework that disentangles disturbances from the underlying clean image. The core mechanism involves a generator that creates noisy images from clean ones, while simultaneously learning to map noisy inputs back to their clean counterparts. This process is governed by a cyclic consistency loss function, ensuring that the generated noisy version of a recreated clean image matches the original input. Additionally, we employ a new multi-variate function loss to enhance the model's ability to handle diverse noise patterns. Experimental results demonstrate that this self-supervised method achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art supervised denoising techniques.

We investigate the challenge of reconstructing a sparse signal from its incomplete linear measurements. This problem is typically resolved via $\ell_1$ minimization, though we demonstrate that for a specific subset of instances, achieving an exact recovery is possible by solving a minimization problem with a constraint on a novel, sparsity-promoting norm. This norm is defined as the infimum of $\ell_1$ norm over all possible extensions of the sparse signal to a more complete measurement set. We establish the theoretical foundation for this norm and provide a proof of a minimum sparsity threshold required to ensure exact recovery.

Engine learning has recently emerged as a promising method for optimizing internal combustion engines, offering a viable alternative to traditional experimental testing. A critical challenge in developing these surrogate models is accurately capturing the complex, non-linear relationship between input parameters and output metrics. We demonstrate that the magnitude of this influence is highly variable across different parameters, with some exhibiting strong effects and others showing negligible ones. Consequently, we propose a new modeling strategy that incorporates end-influence directly into the prediction process. This method yields a significant reduction in modeling error compared to conventional approaches. Furthermore, we examine how end-influence correlates with the selection of training data, identifying specific characteristics of the selected points that enhance prediction accuracy.

This relationship allows for the derivation of a direct link between these parameters and a normalized frequency, which is determined by potential properties independent of temperature. Consequently, a single normalized frequency can fully characterize both the thermal capacity and the effective potential experienced by the particle.

Crowdsourcing has become a prevalent method for gathering data, particularly in natural language processing (NPLP) and related fields. However, this approach often results in noisy datasets where individual contributors exhibit varying levels of expertise and reliability. To address these inconsistencies, this study introduces a novel ensemble modeling framework that integrates uncertainty quantification. The approach employs "human softmax" distributions to represent annotator confidence levels and utilizes entropy metrics to measure uncertainty within the data itself. The proposed framework is evaluated on two established datasets: the WikiAnn dataset for word sense disambiguation and the WikiLing dataset for entity disambiguation. The findings demonstrate that this ensemble method, when combined with human-in-the-loop techniques, significantly outperforms standard majority voting strategies.

This paper introduces an eco-friendly adaptive multiple entry framework designed for decentralized vehicle networks. The approach employs a novel, low-complexity vehicle selection algorithm that ensures fairness among vehicles while maintaining a low average queue length at each entry point. This strategy is designed to minimize the environmental impact of decentralized V2X networks by reducing the frequency of new connection requests, thereby lowering the overall control message traffic. Furthermore, the authors propose a reinforcement learning-based training framework to determine the optimal parameters for this adaptive entry strategy. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average queue length reduction of 10.5% compared to the standard multiple access strategy, with a marginal increase in control message traffic of only 0.5%.

Feature toggles are a software engineering technique that enables the deployment of unfinished functionalities, a capability increasingly vital for the rapid iteration cycles characteristic of modern software development. This study examines the extent to which feature toggles are utilized in open-source environments, specifically focusing on GitHub projects. By analyzing data from 1,000 projects, the research investigates the relationship between the implementation of these features and subsequent code merges, as well as potential design flaws. The findings indicate that while feature toggles are present in a significant number of projects, the majority are managed responsibly with minimal design issues. However, the paper also highlights a critical issue: projects utilizing feature toggles are less likely to experience their code being merged into the main branch. This suggests that although these features facilitate the release of incomplete code, their use does not guarantee that such code will eventually reach a stable, merged state.

This study examines the application of deep learning for classifying point clouds, utilizing a collection of 1,000 cuneiform tablets from the British Museum as a case study. The proposed method employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to categorize point clouds into one of three groups: cuneiform tablets, clay balls, and clay cones. The effectiveness of CNNs is benchmarked against traditional machine learning approaches, specifically Random Forest and Support Vector Machine (SVM). The results indicate that CNNs yield superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 98.4% on the test set. Furthermore, the research investigates the interpretability of CNNs by employing the Grad-CAM technique to generate heatmaps that reveal the specific regions of the point clouds driving the classification decisions.

To achieve this, we developed a novel game-theoretic model that incorporates a specific set of household limitations. Our approach utilizes a game-theoretic framework to analyze these constraints and derive optimal strategies for both parties. Furthermore, we conducted an empirical study to evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed framework and the resulting strategies.

It leverages the established technique of distributed representations for compositional meaning (Gentner & al., 2019), which utilizes associations between word embeddings and role labels to encode the structural relationships among semantic units. This expansion enables the representation of associations between any pair of entities in the scene, leading to a comprehensive distributed depiction of the entire scene. We validate this method using a neural network trained on the COCO dataset, which successfully learns to identify object role associations. Furthermore, we illustrate the framework's utility in reasoning tasks, showing that the learned associations facilitate novel reasoning capabilities.

This shift mimics the effect of a null result in nulling interferometry. To address these issues, we propose using a specific variant of the Michelson interferometer that compensates for this phase shift.

This capability offers a promising pathway for investigating the electronic properties of novel materials under high-pressure conditions.
